titleStmt.author: Shivangi Dhawan

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Online Learning: A Panacea in the Time of COVID-19 Crisis

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: online learning as an emergency substitute for classroom teaching, appraised rather than measured
span.quote: Objectives of the Study To explore the growth of EdTech Start-ups and online learning. To conduct an Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, & Challenges (SWOC) analysis of online learning during the Corona Virus pandemic and natural disasters. To give some suggestions and recommendations for the success of online mode of learning during a crisis-like situation.

span.label: what the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and challenges of online learning are during a crisis, and what institutions should do about them
span.quote: Objectives of the Study To explore the growth of EdTech Start-ups and online learning. To conduct an Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, & Challenges (SWOC) analysis of online learning during the Corona Virus pandemic and natural disasters. To give some suggestions and recommendations for the success of online mode of learning during a crisis-like situation.

span.label: a SWOC appraisal of online learning in the first months of the Covid-19 pandemic, assembled entirely from secondary sources
span.quote: The study is descriptive and tries to understand the importance of online learning in the period of a crisis and pandemics such as the Covid-19. The problems associated with online learning and possible solutions were also identified based on previous studies. The SWOC analysis was conducted to understand various strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and challenges associated with online mode of learning during this critical situation. The research tool used for analyzing the data which amassed from different sources for this study is a content analysis and the research method is descriptive research. We have taken into consideration the qualitative aspects of the research study. This study is completely based on the secondary data.

span.label: an entire education system moved online in weeks, by institutions that had declined to move for years
span.quote: This situation challenged the education system across the world and forced educators to shift to an online mode of teaching overnight. Many academic institutions that were earlier reluctant to change their traditional pedagogical approach had no option but to shift entirely to online teaching

span.quote: Although the availability of electricity and a stable internet connection is still a bigger challenge in their way as a lot of Indian cities especially small cities still face frequent electricity shortages.

span.label: `panacea` - the title's word and the paper's own hedge against it. The body says EdTech `CANNOT REPLACE A TEACHER BUT IT CAN ENHANCE INSTRUCTION`, which is the opposite of a panacea claim, and the title is the part that gets cited
span.quote: EdTech cannot replace a teacher but it can enhance instruction.

span.label: the arguments FOR e-learning, as this paper lists them - accessibility, affordability, flexibility, learning pedagogy, life-long learning, policy. Every one is a property claimed for the mode rather than measured on a cohort
span.quote: Several arguments are associated with e-learning. Accessibility, affordability, flexibility, learning pedagogy, life-long learning, and policy are some of the arguments related to online pedagogy.

span.label: critiques → educational institutions that remained on traditional face-to-face methods and were `stuck with old procedures` until the pandemic removed the choice
span.quote: Educational institutions (schools, colleges, and universities) in India are currently based only on traditional methods of learning, that is, they follow the traditional set up of face-to-face lectures in a classroom. Although many academic units have also started blended learning, still a lot of them are stuck with old procedures.

span.label: critiques → the view that supplying the technology is the problem - the paper says the challenge is `not only finding new technology and using it but also REIMAGINING ITS EDUCATION`
span.quote: The challenge to educational institutions is not only finding new technology and using it but also reimagining its education, thereby helping students and academic staff who are seeking guidance for digital literacy.
